source.title: Evaluation Under Imperfect Benchmarks and Ratings: A Case Study in Text Simplification
source.authors: Joseph Liu; Yoonsoo Nam; Xinyue Cui; Swabha Swayamdipta

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendices are present. Some chart text is garbled in the extraction, but the relevant reported values are also stated in text or the correlation matrix.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether simplification quality scores track model size, using human and LLM ratings rather than measuring pretraining loss or fitting scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper tests model-size trends in text simplification, relevant to V6. It does not test power-law loss scaling, extrapolation of loss, compute-optimal allocation, architectural shape effects, other modalities or training regimes, or fit-dependence of scaling-law exponents. Prior scaling-law findings are cited as motivation, not tested here.
record.test_reason: The study mainly assumes larger models simplify better and uses size as a proxy. Its human pilot (§3.2) tests that assumption directly: three experts rated outputs from four Llama 3 instruct models (1B–70B). That is a downstream-quality-versus-scale result in a new task setting, bearing on V6. Everything else in the paper evaluates the evaluators (metrics and LLM judges), not the models.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SynthSimpliEval, validated by a high-agreement human pilot whose ratings rise with model size, plus an LLMs-as-a-Jury panel, gives reliable simplification evaluation. Existing metrics fail to capture the size trend. A small learnable metric trained on jury-labelled synthetic data improves size correlation (0.22), though it stays well below the jury.
record.recipe_differences: This is a downstream text-simplification evaluation study, not a pretraining-loss scaling-law measurement or reproduction. It compares task-quality ratings across four instruction-tuned Llama 3 model sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: Judge prompt format changes the reported size correlation (0.335 to 0.648 across the shown prompt ablations); temperature changes it from 0.626 at 0.1 to 0.581 at 1.0. The paper says temperature has minimal impact.

fits_no_version.finding: Existing text-simplification metrics fail to track model size: Delta FKGL −0.20, SLE −0.26, LENS 0.04, BERTScore 0.06. LLM judges track it at 0.40–0.63, and their average at 0.68. The correlation depends on the judge prompt (0.335–0.648).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Automatic metrics for generation tasks may not reflect scale-driven quality gains that humans and LLM judges detect.

record.problems: The human pilot covers 20 sentences and three NLP-expert annotators; the size comparison uses only four models from one model family. The study uses model size as a proxy for simplification quality. No uncertainty intervals are reported for the size correlations or mean scores, and several results are presented only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Not stated: no additional results bearing on V6 were left out; rows include the human-pilot means, jury-mean values, correlations in Appendix B, and the reported temperature and prompt ablations.

untested.parts: No other modalities or training regimes.

Untested: any functional form or 'predictable' fit; any link to pretraining loss; other tasks or model families. There are only four models from mixed Llama 3.1/3.2/3.3 releases rather than a controlled scale series.
No exponents or fits are examined.

missing.what: Spearman correlation of 0.759 between human ratings and simplifier model size

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily an evaluation-methodology paper that assumes size implies quality; only the small human pilot bears on V6. The jury results are circular for V6 because the jury setup was ablated to maximise correlation with model size. The four simplifiers come from different Llama releases, so size is confounded with release and training differences.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law relationship in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No small-run loss fits or predictions of larger-run loss are evaluated.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation or compute-optimal split is studied.
The study does not compare depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
The study does not test scaling laws across modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.

Tests text-simplification output quality against model size for four Llama 3 instruction-tuned models; it does not test pretraining loss, other downstream tasks, or a broad range of model families and scales.
No scaling-law exponents, loss-curve bends, or dependence of scaling-law fits on setup choices are examined.

relationships.condition: Expert human ratings (3 annotators, 20 sentences, 80 pairs) of text simplifications from Llama 3.2 1B, 3.2 3B, 3.1 8B and 3.3 70B Instruct
relationships.reason: Mean normalised quality rises monotonically, 0.371→0.575→0.754→0.808, with Spearman 0.759 against size (H1–H4). The trend is monotonic only; no predictive fit.
relationships.display_finding: Mean normalized quality increased from 0.371 to 0.575 to 0.754 to 0.808, with a Spearman correlation of 0.759 against model size.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Human pilot ratings of Llama 3.2 1B, Llama 3.2 3B, Llama 3.1 8B, and Llama 3.3 70B Instruct on SynthSimpliEval
reader_labels.reason: Mean human ratings rise across the four model sizes, and the authors report a Spearman correlation of 0.759 between human ratings and model-size scores (H1-H4).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The jury's mean scores rise across the four simplifier sizes, and its average score has a 0.68 Spearman correlation with model-size scores (A1-A4, M12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Existing automatic simplification metrics and individual LLM judges on SynthSimpliEval
reader_labels.reason: Existing metrics show weak or reversed size correlations, while individual judge correlations vary; the observed predictive trend depends on the evaluator used (M1-M11).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Qwen 2.5 72B Instruct judge prompt and temperature ablations
reader_labels.reason: Correlation with simplifier size changes across prompt choices and decreases somewhat at higher temperatures (P1-P3, T1-T4).
